Skill.constraints[1]: Skill metadata description: Manage issues, projects & team workflows in Linear. Use when the user wants to
read, create or updates tickets in Linear.
Skill.constraints[2]: Skill metadata short-description: Manage Linear issues in Codex
Skill.constraints[4]: Interface short_description: Manage Linear issues in Codex
Skill.constraints[7]: Interface default_prompt: Use Linear context to triage or update relevant issues for this task, with clear next
Skill.constraints[8]: MCP dependency: linear (Linear MCP server), transport streamable_http, url https://mcp.linear.app/mcp.
Skill.constraints[9]: Follow these steps in order. Do not skip steps.
Skill.constraints[10]: Linear MCP server must be connected and accessible via OAuth.
Skill.constraints[11]: Confirm access to the relevant Linear workspace, teams, and projects.
Skill.constraints[12]: Step 0: Set up Linear MCP (if not already configured).
Skill.constraints[13]: If any MCP call fails because Linear MCP is not connected, pause and set it up.
Skill.constraints[14]: Step 1: Clarify the user's goal and scope (e.g., issue triage, sprint planning, documentation audit, workload
balance). Confirm team/project, priority, labels, cycle, and due dates as needed.
Skill.constraints[15]: Step 2: Select the appropriate workflow (see Practical Workflows below) and identify the Linear MCP tools you
will need. Confirm required identifiers (issue ID, project ID, team key) before calling tools.
Skill.constraints[16]: Step 3: Execute Linear MCP tool calls in logical batches: Read first (list/get/search) to build context. Create or
update next (issues, projects, labels, comments) with all required fields. For bulk operations, explain grouping logic before applying
Skill.constraints[17]: Step 4: Summarize results, call out remaining gaps or blockers, and propose next actions (additional issues,
label changes, assignments, or follow-up comments).
Skill.constraints[18]: After successful login, the user will have to restart codex. You should finish your answer and tell them so when
they try again they can continue with Step 1.
